params.desc: If phase "C" is positively energized, and phases "A" and "B" are negatively energized, this logical sensor reads as "1", while others read as "0".

params.name: Hall signals inverted
params.desc: This parameter instructs the servo drive to invert readings of all Hall sensors before mapping them to logical sensors.

sections.name: Peripheral: RC PWM or Electronic Gearing

params.name: enable
params.desc: Turns on the RC PWM control interface or Electronic Gearing interface. Note that both CAN and USB interfaces stop processing commands whenever RC PWM is enabled.

params.name: Function
params.desc: This parameter defines what function the PWM interface performs.

params.name: PWM capture interface
params.desc: The servo drive has two different hardware interfaces for capturing input PWM signals. This parameters tells the device which of the interfaces the RC PWM signal is connected to.

params.name: polarity inversion
params.desc: The parameter tells the device to electrically invert the input PWM signal. Leave the default setting unless an application-specific need arises.

params.name: RC PWM: pulse period
params.desc: This parameter specifies the period of the PWM pulses sent to the servo drive. What matters are the ratios between pulse period, min and max pulse widths, rather than their absolute values. This means that any units (e.g. seconds or clocks) can be used.

params.name: RC PWM: max pulse width (angle=360 deg)
params.desc: This parameter specifies the duty cycle that corresponds to MAXIMUM input. What matters are the ratios between pulse period, min and max pulse widths, rather than their absolute values. This means that any units (e.g. seconds or clocks) can be used.

params.name: RC PWM: min pulse width (angle=0 deg)
params.desc: This parameter specifies the duty cycle that corresponds to ZERO input. What matters are the ratios between pulse period, min and max pulse widths, rather than their absolute values. This means that any units (e.g. seconds or clocks) can be used.

params.name: RC PWM: pulse timeout period
params.desc: The device reports a fault if no pulse is detected within this timeout period. Timeout 0 means "no fault on timeout".

params.name: RC PWM: inverted installation
params.desc: Swap the way the device interprets the max pulse width and min pulse width.

params.name: RC ESC: bidirectional speed
params.desc: This setting is applicable to Electronic Speed Control (ESC) mode of operation. This settings is ignored in Servo Control mode. • 0: unidirectional speed • 1: bidirectional speed

params.name: Electronic Gearing: multiplier
params.desc: The parameters defines how much FASTER the SLAVE motor moves in relation to a MASTER motor.

params.name: Electronic Gearing: divider
params.desc: The parameters defines how much SLOWER the SLAVE motor moves in relation to a MASTER motor.

params.name: Emergency Stop Switch
params.desc: This parameter specifies which GPIO pin is to be used as an Emergency Stop input. Refer to datasheet for a list of available input GPIO pins. If this parameter is set to 0, this means Emergency Stop function is disabled.

params.name: Limit Switch: Negative Speed
params.desc: This parameter specifies which GPIO pin is connected to a limit switch acting in NEGATIVE speed direction. Refer to datasheet for a list of available input GPIO pins. If this parameter is set to 0, this means the function is disabled.

params.name: Limit Switch: Positive Speed
params.desc: This parameter specifies which GPIO pin is connected to a limit switch acting in POSITIVE speed direction. Refer to datasheet for a list of available input GPIO pins. If this parameter is set to 0, this means the function is disabled.

params.name: Switches: type
params.desc: This setting applies to both Limit Switches as well as to the Emergency Stop Switch.

params.name: Generic Output
params.desc: This parameter tells which GPIO pin is to be used to output command-controlled discrete or PWM signal. This signal is typically used to control a solenoid of a brake. Refer to datasheet for a list of available output GPIO pins. If this parameter is set to 0, this means the function is disabled.

params.name: Generic Input
params.desc: This parameter tells which GPIO pin is to be used as a general-purpose input that can be read out via a telemetry interface. Refer to datasheet for a list of available input GPIO pins. If this parameter is set to 0, this means the function is disabled.

params.name: Thermistor: enable
params.desc: This parameter enables an analog interface (pin) to an external Thermistor.

params.name: ADC: Amplifier Gain Selector
params.desc: Use ADC Amplifier to better match the dynamic range of ADC to the range of the motor's phase currents. This increases effective resolution of the ADC output, improves performance of the motor and reduces energy losses due to heating in the motor. If a particular motor has a lower Maximum Continuous Current rating vs. that of the servo drive, then the dynamic range of the servo drive's ADC module is not fully utilized. This under-utilization of the dynamic range creates discretization errors when measuring phase currents. The discretization errors reduces efficiency of the servo drive when controlling small motors. To counter this issue, increase the gain of the amplifier whenever the motor's "Maximum Continuous Current" rating is ~10 times less than the Amps rating of your servo drive. Re-confirm this threshold for your particular model of the servo drive. For example, if your servo drive has a nominal current rating of 60A, then by increasing the gain, you reduce the rating to 60A /4 = 15A and thus improving resolution of the ADC when controlling a low-Amps motor. If your servo drive is a 25A device, then by enabling the amplifier, you get 25A/4 = 6.25A nominal current range.

params.name: ADC: Shunt Resistor in Phase A
params.desc: This is a nominal resistance of a shunt resistor soldered to the PCB. There are just a few cases when this configuration parameter needs to be changed. • whenever a different shunt resistor is soldered to the PCB for circuit optimization purposes, • for calibration purposes to fine-tune current sensing, • when re-flashing the firmware.

params.name: ADC: Shunt Resistor in Phase B
params.desc: This is a nominal resistance of a shunt resistor soldered to the PCB. There are just a few cases when this configuration parameter needs to be changed. • whenever a different shunt resistor is soldered to the PCB for circuit optimization purposes, • for calibration purposes to fine-tune current sensing, • when re-flashing the firmware.

params.name: ADC: Shunt Correction Factor
params.desc: This is an experimentally determined calibration parameter that helps account for non-linearities of phase current measurements. Keep this parameter at its default value unless a calibrated reference current sensor is used for ADC fine-tuning.

params.name: PWM: Period (Inverter Resolution)
params.desc: This parameter defines a period of the inverter's PWM signal. This parameter indirectly defines "inverter resolution". The higher the parameter is, the more precise the inverter is capable of positioning the stator's magnetic field, the lower PWM frequency is, the lower ADC sampling frequency is, and the lower the current control loop's frequency is. Changing this parameter causes obscure side effects. Do not change this parameter unless you know what you are doing.

params.name: PWM: ADC Decimation Factor
params.desc: This parameter defines how often ADC sampling takes place in relation to the inverter's PWM frequency. This also affects current control loop's frequency. Do not change this parameter unless you know what you are doing.

params.name: PWM: Dead Ticks
params.desc: This parameter is dependent on datasheet of MOSFET transistors soldered to the board. Do not change this parameter unless a different set of transistors is soldered to the board. Do not change this parameter unless specifically advised to do so.

params.name: PWM: Minimal Pulse Width
params.desc: This parameter is dependent on datasheet of MOSFET transistors soldered to the board. Do not change this parameter unless a different set of transistors is soldered to the board. Do not change this parameter unless specifically advised to do so.

params.name: Udc capacitor: C
params.desc: This is a nominal capacitance value of a set of capacitors soldered to the PCB. The value is relevant to starter-generator applications only. Keep this parameter at its default value most of the time.

params.name: CAN: bitrate
params.desc: The parameter defines bitrate in kbps for the CAN interface of the servo drive. This bit rate should match the bitrates of other devices on the same CAN network.

params.name: CANopen: Node ID
params.desc: The parameter defines the servo drive's Node ID on a CANopen network. Valid Node IDs range from 1 to 127 (11 bits only). An initial Node ID is automatically generated. The value can be changed here to ensure uniqueness of the Node ID within a CANopen network.

params.name: CANopen: heartbeat timeout
params.desc: If the servo drive does not receive any messages via either CAN or USB interfaces within this time period, the device assumes that there is a problem with a parent control system. Upon detecting a heartbeat timeout event, the servo drive executes the following actions: 1. The servo drive automatically issues a "Stop" command to itself, 2 ......that stops the motor, 3 ......and depending on the configuration, might enable the "Brake" function.

params.name: CANopen: receiving frequency
params.desc: The parameter specifies how often the device reads out incoming CAN/USB messages from network queues. Since the incoming messages usually carry control/reference signals for the device, this parameter indirectly defines the device's control bandwidth and latency. Do not set this parameter higher than actually needed as this causes CPU congestion due to a high number of CPU interrupts.

params.name: CANopen: telemetry frequency
params.desc: The parameter specifies how often the device sends telemetry messages (CANopen TPDO packets) to a parent control system. The servo drive sends a single TPDO message at a time, looping across the messages with a frequency defined by this parameter.

params.name: Feature: USB2CAN routing
params.desc: This feature turns the device into a USB-to-CAN gateway ("USB2CAN dongle" function). Note that enabling the function puts a performance penalty on the servo drive.

params.name: USB2CAN: support 29bit ID frames
params.desc: The parameter enables support for routing of 29bit frames between USB and CAN. If the feature is turned off, the built-in USB-to-CAN gateway routes 11bit frames only.

params.name: USB: serial number
params.desc: The USB serial number is visible to host computers and can be used to identify the device among multiple devices connected to a host. The serial number is automatically generated, but can be changed here if needed.

params.name: Activation Key
params.desc: The activation key is provided by technical support team to the buyer of this device. Follow instructions from technical support team to obtain the activation key.

params.name: Fault Bits
params.desc: Whenever a fault is detected, the servo drive powers off the motor, latches one or more "Fault Bits" flags, and starts waiting for a "Reset" command to come from a parent control system. Until a "Reset" command comes, the servo drive ignores all other commands received from the parent control system. Note that all configuration management functions (CANopen SDO functionality) keep working as usual. The parent control system is expected to continuously monitor the "Fault Bits" parameter delivered to it via CANopen TPDO mechanism. If the "Fault Bits" parameter is 0 (all bits are clear), then nothing needs to be done. Whenever one or more bits of the "Fault Bits" value indicate a fault, the parent control system is supposed to issue a "Reset" command. The "Reset" command needs to be issued once the fault is corrected, and the actuator is ready to re-start operation.

params.name: Operation Mode

options.19: Brushed Motor or Solenoid Control (1-2 motors)

params.desc: This parameter tells what control law the servo drive is currently using to drive the motor.

params.name: Commutation Mode
params.desc: This parameter tells which method the servo drive is currently using to determine electrical position of the rotor.

params.name: Kickstart needed
params.desc: This telemetry parameter tells if the motor needs a kickstart at its current state. A kickstart is needed if a sensorless motor is not yet moving or moving slowly, or if a Motor Encoder with Quadrature interface is yet to find its Index position.

params.name: Electrical Position
params.desc: This telemetry parameter tells the position of the rotor in relation to the stator. This position is measured using Hall sensors or a motor encoder, or estimated by "Sensorless Observer" method.

params.name: Speed (Electrical Frequency)
params.desc: This telemetry parameter tells the speed of the motor's rotor. The speed is defined in electrical revolutions per second (Hz). To convert electrical revolutions per second (Hz) to motor shaft's revolutions per second, just divide it by the number of pole pairs. For example, assuming the speed is 20 Hz (electrical), and Poles Number is 8, then the corresponding speed in motor shaft's revolutions per second is 20 /(8/2) = 5.0 (revolutions per second), which is 5 * 60 = 300 RPM.

params.name: Work Zone: Speed
params.desc: This is the speed of rotation of payload measured using a Servo Encoder or estimated using a Motor Encoder, Hall Sensors or via a sensorless technique.

params.name: Work Zone: Count
params.desc: The "Work Zone: Count" telemetry is the same as "Servo Encoder Counts" except that it continuously spans in both positive and negative directions. This telemetry output is affected by "Work Zone: zero offset" setting as well as by "inverted installation" and "encoder bias vs. electrical position" parameters of the encoder's configuration. The "Work Zone Count" is not limited to Servo Encoder's resolution. Instead, it logically spans in both positive or negative directions as many encoder counts as needed. Both Servo Control and Direct Drive Control use the logical work zone's counts at their references instead of the physical servo encoder's readings. This makes it easier to develop "multi-turn" servo applications.

params.name: Work Zone: Turn Count
params.desc: This telemetry parameter counts full revolutions using the following formula: "Work Zone: Turn Count" = "Work Zone: Count" div "Work Zone: Dimension".

params.name: Work Zone: Modulo Count
params.desc: This is a measurement of a partial revolution as computed using the following modulo division formula: "Work Zone: Modulo" = "Work Zone: Count" mod "Work Zone: Dimension".

params.name: Work Zone: Dimension
params.desc: This is a size of Work Zone defined in Servo Encoder counts. The value is used for computing "Work Zone: Modulo" and "Work Zone: Turn Count". Usually, this size equals the value of "counts per revolution", a parameter of a Servo Encoder. However, it can be configured to be an arbitrary number to simplify application development. For example, for a CNC machine, this value can be set to match a size of the CNC machine's actual work zone measured in Servo Encoder counts.

params.name: Motor Encoder: Counts
params.desc: This is an ABSOLUTE POSITION read out from an encoder that plays the "Motor Encoder" role.

params.name: Servo Encoder: Counts
params.desc: This is an ABSOLUTE POSITION read out from an encoder that plays the "Servo Encoder" role.

params.name: Reference: Current
params.desc: This is the currently active reference, a commanded target, for current flowing through the motor.

params.name: Reference: Speed (Electrical Frequency)
params.desc: This is the currently active reference, a commanded target, for the motor's speed.

params.name: Reference: Work Zone Count
params.desc: This is the currently active reference, a commanded target, for the servo actuator.

params.name: Target Reached
params.desc: This indicator tells if a reference servo position has been reached. This indicator does not latch.

params.name: Sample Number
params.desc: This is a continuously incremented counter of samples taken by an ADC module of the servo drive. The counter is incremented with the sampling frequency of the servo drive.

params.name: Voltage: DC bus (Udc)
params.desc: Measured voltage of the input power supply.

params.name: Voltage: DC bus (Udc, f32)
params.desc: Measured voltage of the input power supply. This is a FLOAT32 version of the measured value (4bytes long).

params.name: Current: DC bus (Itotal)
params.desc: Measured electric current flowing through power supply DC link.

params.name: Current: Phase A (Ia)
params.desc: Measured electric current flowing through phase A.

params.name: Current: Phase B (Ib)
params.desc: Measured electric current flowing through phase B.

params.name: Current: Phase C (Ic)
params.desc: Measured electric current flowing through phase C.

params.name: Thermistor
params.desc: Raw ADC output of measured voltage drop on Thermistor.

params.name: CPU Temperature
params.desc: Measured temperature of the servo drive's CPU.

sections.name: Telemetry - Field Oriented Control: FOC, ESC & Servo

params.name: Torque
params.desc: This is an estimate of TORQUE that the motor is currently generating. Note that this estimation is only available whenever the motor runs under Field Oriented Control (FOC).

params.name: FOC: Iq Current
params.desc: This is an estimate of Iq current derived from phase currents measured by the ADC.

params.name: FOC: Id Current
params.desc: This is an estimate of Id current derived from phase currents measured by the ADC.

params.name: FOC: Uq Output Voltage
params.desc: This is a Uq voltage, an output of a FOC control law.

params.name: FOC: Uq Integral Term
params.desc: This is an integral term of a PI controller that commands Uq voltage to stabilize Iq current.

params.name: FOC: Ud Output Voltage
params.desc: This is a Ud voltage, an output of a FOC control law.

params.name: FOC: Ud Integral Term
params.desc: This is an integral term of a PI controller that commands Ud voltage to stabilize Id current.

params.name: ESC: Integral Term
params.desc: This is an integral term of a PI controller that commands Iq current to stabilize speed.

params.name: Servo: Integral Term
params.desc: This is an integral term of a PID controller that commands speed to stabilize position.

params.name: Direct Field Control: Electrical Position
params.desc: This telemetry parameter tells an estimate of position of the rotor in relation to the stator.

params.name: Direct Field Control: Speed (Electrical Frequency)
params.desc: This telemetry parameter tells an estimate of speed of the motor. The speed is defined in electrical revolutions per second (Hz). To convert electrical revolutions per second (Hz) to motor shaft's revolutions per second, just divide it by the number of pole pairs. For example, assuming the speed is 20 Hz (electrical), and Poles Number is 8, then the corresponding speed in motor shaft's revolutions per second is 20 /(8/2) = 5.0 Hz (revolutions per second), which is 5 * 60 = 300 RPM.

params.name: Sensorless: Speed (Electrical Frequency)
params.desc: This telemetry parameter tells an estimated speed of the "sensorless" motor. The speed is defined in electrical revolutions per second (Hz). To convert electrical revolutions per second (Hz) to motor shaft's revolutions per second, just divide it by the number of pole pairs. For example, assuming the speed is 20 Hz (electrical), and Poles Number is 8, then the corresponding speed in motor shaft's revolutions per second is 20 /(8/2) = 5.0 Hz (revolutions per second), which is 5 * 60 = 300 RPM.

params.name: Sensorless: Electrical Position
params.desc: This telemetry parameter tells an estimated position of the rotor in relation to the stator.

params.name: Sensorless: Emf alpha
params.desc: This is an estimate of Back-Emf voltage (the "sine" component).

params.name: Sensorless: Emf beta
params.desc: This is an estimate of Back-Emf voltage (the "cosine" component).

params.name: Sensorless: Back-Emf Constant (Ke)
params.desc: This is an estimate of "Back-Emf Constant (Ke)" measured in V (peak, line-to-neutral) per electrical rad/s.

params.name: Sensorless: Technical Speed Limit
params.desc: This is an estimate of MAXIMUM speed the "Sensorless Observer" method is capable of measuring. The limit is caused by finite performance of CPU, and a finite sampling frequency of ADC.

params.name: Sensorless: Zero Speed Threshold
params.desc: This is an estimate of MINIMUM speed at which the "Sensorless Observer" method is still capable of sensing Back-Emf voltages in the presence of background noise.

params.name: Hall Observer: Hall code
params.desc: Hall sensors generate 6 codes (counts) per electrical revolution. This telemetry parameter tells the current Hall code.

params.name: Hall Observer: Speed (Electrical Frequency)
params.desc: This telemetry parameter tells an estimated speed of the motor. The speed is defined in electrical revolutions per second (Hz). To convert electrical revolutions per second (Hz) to motor shaft's revolutions per second, just divide it by the number of pole pairs. For example, assuming the speed is 20 Hz (electrical), and Poles Number is 8, then the corresponding speed in motor shaft's revolutions per second is 20 /(8/2) = 5.0 Hz (revolutions per second), which is 5 * 60 = 300 RPM.

params.name: Hall Observer: Electrical Position
params.desc: This telemetry parameter tells an estimated position of the rotor in relation to the stator.

params.name: Hall Observer: between codes counter
params.desc: This is a counter that is reset each time a Hall code changes.

params.name: Hall Observer: Hall errors counter

params.name: Controlword
params.desc: Not part of the Stimita Device Reference - added by a firmware-level binary patch on this specific bench drive (see the sibling SDR-CB-60R-D firmware project). Write to command the drive: 0x0000 = Stop, 0x0006 = Off, 0x000F = Servo (holds the drive's current position). Edge-triggered - the drive only acts when this value actually changes. Bit 7 (Fault reset) does not perform a real fault-clearing reset; it is simplified to the same safe state as Off.

params.name: Statusword
params.desc: Not part of the Stimita Device Reference - added by the same firmware patch as Controlword. Computed fresh every cycle: bits 0/1/2/5 (Operation enabled) when Operation Mode >= 4; bits 0/1/5 (Switched on) for Virtual Brake; bit 3 (Fault) when Fault Bits has any bit set other than the one maskable Warning bit; bit 4 (Voltage enabled) from STO status - polarity unverified; bit 6 (Switch on disabled) is the default/idle fallback; bit 7 (Warning) from the maskable Fault Bits bit. Quick-Stop-Active is not separately reported.
